exampleAnswers.title: Describing the General Properties of the Cosecant Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\csc x?$

  1. The point $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right) $ is in the graph of the function.
  2. The function is decreasing on the interval $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).$
  3. $x = -\pi$ is a zero of the function.
question.explanation:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\csc x.$

Now, let's go through each statement.

  • From the graph we see that $\csc\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1.$ Hence, statement I is false.

  • The function $y=\csc x$ is decreasing on the interval $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and increasing on the interval $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right).$ Hence, statement II is true.

  • The function $y=\csc x$ is not defined at $x=-\pi.$ Hence, statement III is false.

example.title: Describing the General Properties of the Cosecant Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\csc x?$

  1. The range of the function is $[-1,1]$
  2. The function is increasing on the interval $(0,\pi).$
  3. The function doesn't have a maximum value.
question.explanation:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\csc x.$

Now, let's go through each statement.

  • The range of the function is $(-\infty,-1]\cup [1,\infty).$ Hence, statement I is false.

  • The function $y=\csc x$ is decreasing on the interval $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and increasing on the interval $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right).$ Hence, statement II is false.

  • The range of the function is $(-\infty,-1]\cup [1,\infty)$, therefore the function doesn't have a maximum value. Hence, statement III is true.

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Cosecant Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \csc x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

\[ \csc{x} = \csc{(x+2n\pi)} . \]

Substituting $n=-3$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

\begin{align*} \csc{x} = \csc{(x+2\cdot (-3)\cdot\pi)} = \csc(x-6\pi) . \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\csc{x} = -3,$ then $\csc{(x-6\pi)} = -3.$

Finally, then

\begin{align} 3\csc(x-6\pi)+4 & = 3 (-3) +4 \\[5pt] &=-9 +4 \\[5pt] &= -5 . \end{align}

example.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Cosecant Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \csc x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

\[ \csc{x} = \csc{(x+2n\pi)} . \]

Substituting $n=-2$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

\begin{align*} \csc{x} = \csc{(x+2\cdot (-2)\cdot\pi)} = \csc(x-4\pi) . \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\csc{x} = 2,$ then $\csc{(x-4\pi)} = 2.$

Finally, then

\begin{align} \dfrac 1 4\csc(x-4\pi)+2& = \dfrac 1 4 (2) +2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 2 +2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 5 2 . \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Oddness Property of the Cosecant Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y = \csc{x}.$

From the graph, we note the following:

  • The period of $\csc{x}$ is $2\pi.$

  • Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\csc{x}$ is an odd function, and we have \[ \csc(-x) = -\csc{x}. \]

Let's now evaluate our expression:

  • Firstly, using the periodicity of $\csc{x},$ we have \begin{align} \csc(-a - 16\pi) & = \csc(-a - 2\pi \cdot 8) \\[5pt] & = \csc(-a). \end{align}

  • Secondly, using the oddness of $\csc{x},$ we have \begin{align} \csc(-a) & = -\csc{a} \\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{9}{4}. \end{align}

Therefore, $\csc(-a - 16\pi) = -\dfrac{9}{4}.$

example.title: Utilizing the Oddness Property of the Cosecant Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y = \csc{x}.$

From the graph, we note the following:

  • The period of $\csc{x}$ is $2\pi.$

  • Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\csc{x}$ is an odd function, and we have \[ \csc(-x) = -\csc{x}. \]

Let's now evaluate our expression:

  • Firstly, using the periodicity of $\csc{x},$ we have \begin{align} \csc(-x + 6\pi) & = \csc(-x + 2\pi \cdot 3) \\[5pt] & = \csc(-x). \end{align}

  • Secondly, using the oddness of $\csc{x},$ we have \begin{align} \csc(-x) & = -\csc{x} \\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{7}{6}. \end{align}

Therefore, \begin{align} 4\csc(-x + 6\pi) + 1 & = 4\left(-\dfrac{7}{6}\right) + 1\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{14}{3} + 1 \\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{11}{3}. \end{align}
